applicable_when: The kernel is L1/shared-memory bound with 8-way bank conflicts on 70% of shared loads (64.81% estimated speedup). Occupancy is crushed to 18.75% by 168 registers/thread (block limit = 3 blocks/SM). The current kernel uses raw pointer arithmetic with manual index computation for A and B tiles, which (a) generates heavy address-computation register pressure and (b) results in non-coalesced shared memory access patterns. On Hopper H200, replacing scalar pointer loads with tl.make_block_ptr + tl.load(..., boundary_check=...) maps to TMA hardware descriptors: address generation is offloaded to a dedicated unit, bulk async copies bypass the scalar load path, and the access pattern is inherently coalesced, directly attacking the UncoalescedSharedAccess and SharedMemoryConflicts rules. Simultaneously reducing BLOCK_M from 128 to 64 halves register pressure, allowing more blocks/SM and improving occupancy.
